description: Canal-belt gable houses of the late 17th-18th c. (Herengracht 251, 261; Keizersgracht and Prinsengracht narrow fronts): 4.2-6.6 m fronts of dark brown brick (often painted), a ground storey (house door or a white timber shop pui) and three or four upper storeys of two or three axes of white-framed sashes with white sills, under a neck or bell gable rising 3-4.5 m over the gable foot with one attic light and a hoist beam

match.note: Herengracht 251 (171304) and 261 (177169), 2021-01-22 strip at 40 px/m: 251 gable foot 15.6 m, bell top 20.0 m over a ground and four upper storeys; 261 gable foot 12.9 m, bell top 17.0 m, ground storey to 4.8 m. BAG years 1640-1741 (the cores); the skyline crown decides neck vs bell (crownMatch). No crownMatch: canal trees reach over the gables on the winter strips (Keizersgracht 250: skyline rise 8.2 m); the crown is pinned per pand

neck.note: a neck gable with white sandstone claw pieces on its shoulders, one large light just over the shoulders and the hoist beam; Keizersgracht 256 (169390), 2021-01-22 strip gridded at 2x (grid-crop 1815-2285): shoulders and side cornices at 14.1 m, the light 14.25-15.9 m and 1.3 m wide, neck to 16.9 m, cap to about 17.5 m (carving to 17.9 m)

bell.note: Herengracht 251 (171304): a bell gable 15.6-20.0 m with one attic light 16.7-17.8 m

low-bell.note: Keizersgracht 254 (169444), 2021-01-22 strip: a broad raised bell with a round cap only about 2 m over the gable foot

tall-neck.note: Keizersgracht 250 (169114), 2021-01-22 strip gridded at 2x (grid-crop 2495-2735): claw pieces 10.7-11.8 m, a light 10.65-12.3 m standing on the gable foot, the neck to 14.5 m under a cap to 15.25 m

tall-neck-small-light.note: Keizersgracht 242 (169118), 2021-01-22 strip gridded at 2x (grid-crop 3400-3640): claw pieces 13.05-13.8 m, a light 13.3-14.5 m, the neck and its round cap to 17.3 m; the light's foot on the gable foot (the round-2 sheet drew it 0.5 m high at sill 0.2)

door-left.note: house door on the left axis; a pand whose door reads on the right is mirrored (mirrorForDoor), so a two-axis front keeps a valid door bay

rhythm.groundFloor: a house door and windows, or a small shop
rhythm.roofline: neck or bell gable with one attic light and a hoist beam
schemaLimits: the claw pieces are drawn as the kit's flat wing pieces with scroll tips; their carving and the cap's crest ornament are not drawn
the white timber shop pui of Herengracht 261 is the auto-placed shopfront
